name: K-Means Clustering
short_description: Partitions data into K non-overlapping clusters by iteratively assigning samples to closest centroids.
intuition: Scatters K pins randomly, pulls points into the nearest pin's group, recalculates the center of each group, and repeats until pins stop moving.
step_by_step_working: Standardize all feature variables.
Initialize K cluster centroids using k-means++.
Assign each sample to its nearest centroid based on Euclidean distance.
Recompute centroids as the mean of assigned data points.
Repeat until assignments stabilize or maximum iterations are reached.

parameters.name: n_clusters
parameters.description: The number of clusters to form as well as the number of centroids to generate.

advantages: Fast convergence and intuitive cluster centers.
limitations: Number of clusters K must be chosen in advance.
when_to_use: When clusters are approximately spherical and well-separated.
When an initial exploratory clustering is needed quickly.
when_to_avoid: When clusters have irregular shapes, rings, or widely differing densities.
python_snippet:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)
code_explanation: Fits K-Means and returns cluster label assignments for each point.

name: Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering
short_description: Bottom-up hierarchical clustering that successively merges closest pairs of clusters into a tree (dendrogram).
intuition: Every point starts as its own tiny cluster. At each step, the two closest clusters merge into one, building an entire family tree of clusters.
step_by_step_working: Compute pairwise distance matrix between all samples.
Assign each sample to its own cluster of size 1.
Find the two clusters with the minimum linkage distance (Ward, complete, or average).
Merge them into a single parent cluster.
Repeat until all samples belong to one root cluster; cut tree at desired height.

parameters.name: n_clusters
parameters.description: The number of clusters to find.

advantages: Produces an interpretable dendrogram tree showing data hierarchies at all granularities.
No initial random centroid seeding needed.
limitations: Computationally heavy: O(n^2) memory and O(n^3) time complexity; fails on large datasets.
use_cases: Phylogenetic biology and evolutionary taxonomy trees.
when_to_use: When hierarchical relationships and dendrogram visualizations are required.
when_to_avoid: On large datasets with tens of thousands of samples.
python_snippet:
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
model = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=3, linkage='ward')
labels = model.fit_predict(X_scaled)
code_explanation: Fits hierarchical clustering using Ward linkage.

name: DBSCAN
short_description: Density-Based Spatial Clustering finding core samples of high density and expanding clusters, flagging outliers as noise.
intuition: Walks through crowded areas. If a point has enough neighbors within reach (eps), it starts a cluster and keeps pulling in neighboring crowded points. Isolated loners are marked as noise.
step_by_step_working: For each point, count neighbors within radius eps.
If count >= min_samples, designate point as a Core Point and start a new cluster.
Iteratively collect all density-reachable points from core points.
Border points within eps of a core point join the cluster.
Any point not reachable from any core point is labeled as noise (-1).

parameters.name: eps
parameters.description: The maximum distance between two samples for one to be considered as in the neighborhood of the other.

parameters.name: min_samples
parameters.description: The number of samples in a neighborhood for a point to be considered as a core point.

advantages: Does not require pre-specifying the number of clusters.
Discovers arbitrarily shaped clusters (e.g. concentric circles or moons).
Explicitly isolates and flags noisy anomaly outliers.
limitations: Sensitive to the choice of eps and min_samples.
Struggles when clusters have substantially different densities.
use_cases: GPS spatial anomaly and traffic congestion cluster discovery.
when_to_use: When clusters have irregular non-spherical shapes.
When robust outlier and noise detection is required.
when_to_avoid: When data has varying density gradients or very high dimensions.
python_snippet:
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN
db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
labels = db.fit_predict(X_scaled)
code_explanation: Identifies dense clusters and assigns noise points a label of -1.

name: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
short_description: Projects high-dimensional data onto orthogonal axes that maximize dataset variance.
intuition: Finds the best angles to view a 3D or high-dimensional object so you can see almost all its structure in a flat 2D shadow.
step_by_step_working: Standardize features to zero mean and unit variance.
Compute covariance matrix of standardized features.
Compute eigenvectors and eigenvalues via SVD.
Sort components by descending eigenvalue magnitude.
Transform dataset into reduced principal component coordinates.

parameters.name: n_components
parameters.description: Number of principal components to keep.

advantages: Drastically reduces storage and compute time for downstream ML models.
Eliminates multicollinearity completely by creating orthogonal features.
limitations: Composite components are harder to interpret than original named features.
use_cases: Visualizing high-dimensional customer or genomic profiles in 2D/3D.
Preprocessing collinear features before regression modeling.
when_to_use: When you have dozens or hundreds of correlated features.
When you need to visualize multi-dimensional data.
when_to_avoid: When individual original feature names and units must be preserved for compliance.
python_snippet:
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)
code_explanation: Projects scaled data onto the top 2 principal components.
